title: Count Visited Nodes in a Directed Graph
statement:
A directed graph has `n` nodes labeled `0` to `n - 1`, and each node has exactly one outgoing edge: node `i` points to node `edges[i]`, which is never `i` itself.

A walk from a start node follows outgoing edges one after another and stops the moment it would step onto a node it has already been on during this same walk. Return an array `answer` of length `n` where `answer[i]` is the number of distinct nodes the walk starting at node `i` passes through, counting node `i` itself.
notes:
## Intuition

Every node has exactly one way out, so any walk eventually falls into a cycle and goes round it once. A node on a cycle sees exactly the nodes of its cycle. A node off the cycles sees itself plus everything its successor sees, so its answer is one more than its successor's. Simulating the walk from every node is O(n²); the trick is to find the cycle nodes first and then fill the others in the right order.

## Approach

1. Count each node's `indegree` (how many edges point into it).
2. Run Kahn's topological peeling: put every node with indegree 0 into `order`, and each time a node is taken, lower its successor's indegree, adding the successor once it reaches 0. Only cycle nodes are never peeled, because each keeps the edge from its cycle predecessor.
3. For each unpeeled node whose answer is still 0, walk its `cycle` once and give every node on it `cycle.length`.
4. Go through `order` backwards. A node's successor comes later in `order` or lies on a cycle, so its answer is already known: `answer[node] = answer[edges[node]] + 1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`edges = [1, 2, 0, 0]` gives indegrees `[2, 1, 1, 0]`. Node 3 starts `order`; removing it drops node 0 to indegree 1, so nothing else is peeled. Nodes 0, 1, 2 remain: from 0 the walk 0 → 1 → 2 → 0 has length 3, so they all get 3. Backwards over `order = [3]`: `answer[3] = answer[0] + 1 = 4`. Result `[3, 3, 3, 4]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each node is peeled at most once and each cycle is walked once.
- Space: O(n) for `indegree`, `order` and `answer`.

## Pitfalls

- Walking every start separately with a visited set is quadratic on a long chain into a cycle.
- Fill tail nodes in reverse peeling order; a forward pass would read successors that are not set yet.
- Mark a whole cycle at once and skip nodes whose answer is already set, or each cycle gets walked many times.
- The graph can have several separate components, each with its own cycle.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `indegree` | edges still pointing into each node; stays above 0 only on cycles |
| `order` | peeled (non-cycle) nodes in topological order |
| `head` | position in `order` of the node being peeled |
| `i`, `node` | index in `order` and the node there during the backward pass |
| `answer` | number of distinct nodes visited from each start |
| `cycle` | the nodes of one cycle, collected by walking it once |
